narrative:
The 2021 Cleveland Guardians — still playing as the Indians for most of the year — entered the season with measured expectations, and April delivered exactly that: a .500 month punctuated by José Ramírez's early heroics and some early bullpen shakiness. The team found its footing in May and June, surging above .500 on the strength of timely hitting from unlikely heroes like René Rivera and Eddie Rosario, building genuine hope that Cleveland could compete in a wide-open AL Central.

July proved to be the turning point where the season's character was truly revealed. A brutal 9-15 record reflected a month of agonizing close losses — Emmanuel Clase and Bryan Shaw surrendering leads, Roberto Pérez bunting into double plays in crucial moments — even as individual brilliance from Pérez's three-run homer and Franmil Reyes' booming shots kept the faithful believing. The team was simultaneously capable of electric baseball and heartbreaking collapses, often in the same week.

August offered a reprieve of sorts, with the club going 14-14 and stabilizing, but the bullpen continued to bleed games in the margins. Wittgren and Karinchak gave up critical homers that kept Cleveland from building any real momentum. By the time September arrived, the math was unforgiving — the Guardians went 13-17 in the final full month, watching their slim playoff hopes dissolve one late-inning implosion at a time, though Owen Miller's clutch single in late September offered a fleeting reminder of what might have been.

Finishing 80-82, Cleveland ended the year two games below .500 — close enough to the playoff picture to sting, far enough away to demand reflection. The pitching staff's 4.34 ERA was serviceable but not dominant, and a team that hit 203 home runs still couldn't outscore opponents over a full season. The 2021 season was a story of promise unfulfilled: a club talented enough to win on any given night, but not quite consistent enough to sustain a run over 162 games.

chapters.description: Cleveland breaks even in April with Ramírez's early power setting the tone, but the bullpen shows vulnerability right away.

chapters.title: Summer Surge
chapters.description: A winning May and June fueled by clutch hits from Rivera and Rosario raises playoff hopes across Cleveland.

chapters.title: July's Cruel Mathematics
chapters.description: A 9-15 July exposes the team's fatal flaw — a bullpen that surrenders leads in the most painful ways possible.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: A 14-14 August keeps Cleveland technically alive but the relief corps continues to give away winnable games.

chapters.title: Fading in September
chapters.description: A 13-17 September closes the door on playoff dreams, though Miller's late clutch single provides a brief, bittersweet spark.
